evidence: empty_void: seg3:end is two tiny mascots and two hairline rules on an otherwise black frame, and seg4:start/seg4:end shrink the whole chart into the upper third leaving the bottom ~40% of the frame empty; seg0 also leaves a dead black band below the source line.

weakest_scene.visible_evidence: At seg2:mid and seg2:end the two series labels are drawn at the same y and overlap character-for-character ('AI over a human for a serious talk 33%' stamped over 'Shared personal info with an AI compa'), and the right-hand label runs off the frame edge; at seg2:start the two circle labels also collide with each other under the bubbles.
weakest_scene.root_cause: The dot-plot/lollipop machine places each row label at the mark's own y with no collision resolution and no measured text extent against the frame width, so as the two values converge (33% vs 25%, '8% apart') the labels land on the same line and overflow the right margin.
weakest_scene.repair_goal: Lay the two series labels out with measured widths and enforced vertical separation inside the safe area — one label above its mark, one below, each truncated/wrapped to fit the frame — so both series names and both values are readable at arm's length, and the value sits next to its own mark rather than in a shared text run.
